newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela likely to issue treasury bills this year.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela likely to issue treasury bills this year.

text.p: The Venezuelan government will probably issue treasury bills before the end of the year to roll over about 165 billion bolivars ($348 million) of debt expiring soon, a top Central Bank official said Wednesday.

"The idea is that the government will go to the market once again to roll over debt which is expiring to relieve us of this pressure and help control liquidity," Manuel Lago Rodriguez, vice president of Central Bank studies told reporters in Congress.
A final decision on the issue, the first in months, should be taken by next week, Lago said.
Better-than-expected government finances, reflecting high oil prices, have allowed the government to make fewer-than-usual treasury bill issues in 1996.
Lago said about only about 45 billion bolivars ($95 million) of treasury bills was currently outstanding.

Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar told a meeting with Venezuela's Foreign Press Association earlier Wednesday that the public sector would finish the year with a surplus equivalent to one percent of gross domestic product.
